citation.author: Elpidorou, Andreas
citation.title: Boredom, as a Concept in Phenomenology
citation.in: de Warren, N. and Toadvine, T. (eds.), Encyclopedia of Phenomenology (Springer Nature Switzerland AG), DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-47253-5_104-1
citation.sourceFileNote: source PDF filename misspells the title as 'Boredome'; in-text title and running head both read 'Boredom, as a Concept in Phenomenology' -- confirmed against the byline page

discipline: philosophy (phenomenology) -- comparative survey of Husserl, Heidegger, and Sartre on boredom
thesis: Presents three phenomenological perspectives on boredom -- an original Husserlian construction via inner time-consciousness, Heidegger's tripartite FCM account (the most sustained and ontologically ambitious of the three), and a Sartrean extension of the Sketch for a Theory of Emotions' functional account of emotion -- to show both what boredom is according to phenomenology and what a phenomenology of boredom reveals about human existence generally.
sections: Definition / Introduction (p.1) -- boredom's phenomenological stakes (meaninglessness, impaired agency, attentional lapses, altered time-perception); three-perspective plan

Boredom and Husserl (pp.1-3) -- original construction (not Husserl's own topic) via inner time-consciousness: retention, primal impression, protention, the living present; melody example; boredom as blurring of the tripartite structure
Boredom and Heidegger (pp.3-6) -- FCM's three forms (being-bored-by, being-bored-with, profound boredom) keyed to Befindlichkeit/Grundstimmung background from Being and Time

Boredom and Sartre (pp.6-8) -- Nausea's Roquentin; Sketch for a Theory of Emotions (STE) extended to boredom (Sartre himself never discusses boredom in STE); bored-student vignette; apathetic vs. agitated boredom (Greenson 1953)

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: organizing thread across all three thinkers: Husserl's blurred living present grounds time 'dragging'; Heidegger's three forms are each defined by a distinctive mode of time's passing

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form)
constructs.treatment: glossed as the most familiar, ordinary-experience form (waiting room, repetitive task); leaves us empty and holds us in limbo via a slower passage of time and deferred goals

constructs.label: being-bored-with (2nd form)
constructs.treatment: dinner-party example; retrospectively recognized as boring because inauthentic/not our own; transforms our relation to time rather than merely dragging it

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: treated at greatest length: impersonal 'es ist einem langweilig,' 'undifferentiated no one,' total withdrawal of significance from past/present/future, disclosed as revelatory Grundstimmung rather than pathology

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: recurs across all three registers: Husserl's empty/unmemorable now, Heidegger's banal dinner party and total withdrawal of significance, Sartre's insignificant/banal/meaningless lecture material

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: central to the Husserlian construction: boredom glossed as consciousness failing to attend to, or be affected by, its object, weakening primal impression/retention/protention together

constructs.label: mind-wandering / task-unrelated thought
constructs.treatment: appears explicitly, though only in the Sartre section's bored-student vignette: boredom motivates the subject to mind wander, doodle, talk to classmates, look outside the window

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: the entry's Sartrean payoff: boredom as an embodied, unreflective attempt to resolve a pressing difficulty, an active attempt to re-establish a proper cognitive relationship to the world; explicitly continuous with the author's own regulatory-theory paper (bor-sec-25)

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: light touch: citation of individuals with a high propensity to boredom who show characteristic duration-estimation errors, a trait-adjacent aside subordinated to the entry's dominantly situational/state analyses

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: never named as such (no citation of Csikszentmihalyi or 'flow'), but functions throughout as boredom's implicit negative-defining contrast -- boring objects repeatedly fail to 'engage,' 'engross,' or 'absorb' us

measures.label: behavioral (RT / errors / performance-monitoring)
measures.treatment: Danckert and Allman (2005) cited for boredom-prone individuals' errors in estimating perceptual-event duration -- the entry's nearest approach to a 'measure,' reported as literature evidence, not first-party data

measures.label: self-report / survey scale
measures.treatment: first-person qualitative reports of time 'stalling' (Martin, Sadlo, and Stew 2006) treated as evidentiary support; qualitative-interview data functioning as the nearest self-report analogue, literature-cited rather than administered

readings.summary: Paraphrases Heidegger's diagnosis of the first form as boredom's most familiar register, tied to a determinate boring thing and a bounded, dragging interval of waiting; a faithful compression without engaging fcm-04's own methodological detail (the anti-consciousness directive, the train-station scene).
readings.tag: P/anticipatory-application (unit-pointer only; not a claim Elpidorou makes about fcm-04's specific sections)

readings.summary: Stays close to Heidegger's own dinner-party example and the retrospective, 'arises from Dasein itself' character of the second form; does not engage FCM's own 'standing present' (stehendes Jetzt) terminology.

Center of gravity of the Heidegger section: the impersonal 'es ist einem langweilig' (quoting p.134), the 'undifferentiated no one' (quoting p.135), the merging of the three temporal dimensions into an 'unarticulated unity' (quoting p.148), and the telling refusal (Versagen) that becomes a telling (Sagen) disclosing Dasein's freedom/ability-to-be (citing pp.140, 148-52).

concepts: retention / primal impression / protention (Husserl's tripartite living present)
Lange-weile ('long while') as the temporal cash-out of a blurred living present
Befindlichkeit and Grundstimmung (fundamental mood/attunement) inherited from Being and Time
Leergelassenheit (being left empty) and Hingehaltenheit (being held in limbo) -- the two structural moments common to all three FCM forms
es ist einem langweilig ('it is boring for one') -- the impersonal subject of profound boredom
Versagen / Sagen (telling refusal) -- profound boredom's revelatory reversal
emotions as 'apprehending the world' / modifications of being-in-the-world (Sartre, STE)
magical transformation of the world (Sartre's account of emotion as changing consciousness of, not the structure of, the world)
interlocutors: Edmund Husserl -- On the Phenomenology of the Consciousness of Internal Time (1991); topic constructed by Elpidorou, not Husserl's own
Martin Heidegger -- FCM (1995, primary target of the Heidegger section) and Being and Time (1962, background architecture)
Jean-Paul Sartre -- Nausea (1938) and Sketch for a Theory of Emotions (2002); also The Family Idiot (1981-93), engaged only briefly
Harvey London and Lenore Monello (1974) -- cognitive manipulation of time-perception producing boredom
James Danckert and Ava-Ann Allman (2005) -- duration-estimation errors in boredom-prone individuals
Marion Martin, Gaynor Sadlo, and Graham Stew (2006) -- first-person qualitative reports of boredom's temporal 'stalling'
Martin Wangh (1975) -- 'endless present' characterization of boredom, quoted
Ralph Greenson (1953) -- apathetic vs. agitated boredom distinction
Wendell O'Brien (2014) -- cited alongside Martin et al. on the apathetic/agitated distinction
Andreas Elpidorou (2015) -- 'The Significance of Boredom: A Sartrean Reading'; the author's own earlier Sartrean piece, NOT itself a unit in this cluster (external self-citation)
tensions: Deficit/aversive framing (Husserl's and Heidegger's registers foreground boredom as an unpleasant collapse of engagement or of temporal/existential meaning) vs. functional/regulatory framing (the Sartrean extension recasts the same phenomenon as a purposive, adaptive response) -- the entry moves through both without adjudicating which is more fundamental; resonates with, and is explicitly continuous with, the cluster's 'boredom-as-deficit <-> boredom-as-functional/adaptive' debate axis (grounded primarily in bor-sec-25/26).

Situational vs. trait framing -- the entry is overwhelmingly situational/state in its analyses (a station wait, a dinner party, a difficult lecture) but concedes, in one aside, a trait-like individual-differences finding (boredom-prone individuals' duration-estimation errors) without reconciling the two registers.

Unified vs. plural boredom -- the entry treats 'boredom' as genuinely three different phenomena under Heidegger (situational, retrospective-inauthentic, profound-ontological) while treating Husserl's and Sartre's constructions as accounts of a single, more unified (ordinary/everyday) boredom; it does not explicitly flag this asymmetry.
